attributes.description: The Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MSRP) for the SKU at the time of allocation. Used for IMU (Initial Markup) calculation, markdown planning, and sell-through rate (STR) analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Price Management; FTC Pricing Guidelines

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for merchandiser or planner annotations on this allocation detail line. May include special handling instructions, buyer comments, or cross-reference notes to T&A (Time and Action) calendar events.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Allocation Module

attributes.name: otif_status
attributes.description: OTIF (On Time In Full) compliance status for this allocation detail line, assessed after actual shipment and receipt. Classifies delivery performance against planned ship and receipt dates and quantities. Critical KPI for supply chain SLA (Service Level Agreement) reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: on_time_in_full|on_time_short|late_in_full|late_short|not_shipped — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS – OTIF Reporting; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: pack_config_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the pre-pack or inner-pack configuration for this allocation line (e.g., size ratio pack, color assortment pack). Applicable when is_pre_pack is true. Drives carton-level fulfillment logic in Manhattan Associates WMS.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS – Pack Configuration; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_qty
attributes.description: The number of units originally planned for allocation to the destination location for this SKU within the allocation plan. Represents the merchandiser's intended distribution quantity before any adjustments.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Allocation Module; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: planned_receipt_date
attributes.description: The expected date on which the destination location (store or DC) is scheduled to receive the allocated units. Drives store receiving workflows and floor-set planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Allocation Module; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: planned_ship_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which allocated units are planned to ship from the distribution center or warehouse to the destination location. Used for OTIF (On Time In Full) tracking and T&A (Time and Action) calendar management.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS – Fulfillment; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: priority_rank
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking assigned to this allocation detail line when inventory is constrained and cannot fulfill all planned allocations. Lower values indicate higher priority. Used by Oracle Retail Merchandising System to sequence fulfillment when ATS (Available to Sell) is insufficient.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Allocation Module

attributes.name: qty_variance
attributes.description: The difference between approved allocation quantity and actual shipped quantity (approved_qty minus shipped_qty). Negative values indicate under-shipment; positive values indicate over-shipment. Used for allocation accuracy KPI reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Allocation Module; Anaplan

attributes.name: received_qty
attributes.description: The actual number of units confirmed as received at the destination location. May differ from shipped quantity due to transit damage, short shipments, or receiving discrepancies.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS – Receiving; SAP Customer Activity Repository – Store Operations

attributes.name: rfid_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) tagging is required for units in this allocation line. When true, Manhattan Associates WMS triggers RFID encoding workflows during pick-and-pack operations.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS – RFID Operations; GS1 RFID Standards

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: The merchandise season code associated with this allocation (e.g., SS24 for Spring/Summer 2024, FW24 for Fall/Winter 2024). Aligns allocation activity with collection planning cycles and OTB (Open-to-Buy) budgets in Anaplan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Assortment Planning; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: shipped_qty
attributes.description: The actual number of units physically shipped from the distribution center to the destination location. Captured from Manhattan Associates WMS shipment confirmation and used for OTIF and variance analysis.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS – Fulfillment; SAP S/4HANA WM

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated this allocation detail record: ORM (Oracle Retail Merchandising System), SAP (SAP S/4HANA), ANAPLAN (Anaplan Merchandise Planning), or MANUAL (planner-entered). Supports data lineage and audit traceability in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; SAP S/4HANA; Anaplan

attributes.name: subclass_code
attributes.description: Merchandise subclass code providing the most granular product classification level within the department-class hierarchy (e.g., T-Shirts, Denim Jeans, Running Shoes). Enables granular allocation and STR (Sell-Through Rate) analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Merchandise Hierarchy

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: The Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) per unit for this SKU at the time of allocation, expressed in the operating currency. Used for inventory valuation, GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) analysis, and financial reporting under IFRS/GAAP.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO – Inventory Valuation; IFRS IAS 2 Inventories; GAAP ASC 330

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this allocation detail record was last modified in the source system. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); IFRS Audit Requirements

attributes.name: wos_target
attributes.description: The target Weeks of Supply (WOS) for the destination location at the time of allocation, representing the number of weeks the allocated inventory is expected to cover based on forecasted sales rate. Used for replenishment planning and NOS (Never Out of Stock) management.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System – Allocation Module; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

products.name: merchandise_financial_plan
products.description: Merchandise financial plan (MFP) capturing top-down and channel-level financial targets for a season by department, class, and distribution channel (DTC retail, DTC e-commerce, wholesale, outlet). Includes planned net sales, planned COGS, planned gross margin, planned GMROI, planned inventory turns, planned markdown dollars, channel-specific pricing strategy, and channel inventory allocation percentages. Serves as the financial planning backbone and GMROI target-setting mechanism for the merchandising organization. Managed in Anaplan.

attributes.name: merchandise_financial_plan_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the merchandise financial plan record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sourcing.sourcing_agreement. Business justification: Financial plans reference sourcing agreements to model committed costs, capacity constraints, and pricing tiers. Essential for financial planning accuracy, ensuring planned COGS and receipts align wit

attributes.name: budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget. Business justification: MFP is the merchandise budget itself; must link to finance budget master for consolidation. Corporate financial planning requires integrating merchandise financial plans into overall budget framework

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: MFP planned costs (COGS, markdowns, shrink) are allocated to cost centers for departmental accountability. Finance requires this link to track planned vs actual expenses by cost center for P&L varianc

attributes.name: customer_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.segment. Business justification: Financial plans forecast revenue by target customer segment. Segment penetration, wallet share, and growth projections drive OTB budgets and investment allocation across categories. Essential for segm

attributes.name: financial_planner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Merchandise financial plans are owned by financial planning analysts who forecast sales, margin, and inventory targets. Critical for approval workflows, forecast accuracy tracking, and planner perform

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: MFP planned revenue and margin are tracked via profit centers by channel/brand. Financial reporting requires linking merchandise financial plans to profit centers for segment P&L planning and performa

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Merchandise financial plans are seasonal planning entities; season_code and season_year exist but no FK to season master. Adding season_id FK normalizes season reference and removes redundant attribut

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the merchandising leader or finance officer who formally approved this merchandise financial plan.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Workday HCM

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: The date on which the merchandise financial plan was formally approved by the merchandising leadership and finance team. Required for audit trail and OTB budget release.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; IFRS/GAAP

attributes.name: channel_inventory_allocation_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of total planned inventory allocated to this specific distribution channel (DTC retail, DTC e-commerce, wholesale, outlet). Drives channel-level receipt planning and allocation strategies in Oracle Retail.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System Allocation; Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module

attributes.name: class_code
attributes.description: Merchandise class code within the department hierarchy (e.g., Denim, Knitwear, Running Shoes). Represents the second level of the Oracle Retail merchandise hierarchy below department.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this merchandise financial plan record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which all monetary plan values are expressed (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Supports multi-currency planning for international wholesale and DTC channels.

attributes.name: department_code
attributes.description: Merchandise department code to which this financial plan applies (e.g., Womens Apparel, Mens Footwear, Accessories). Aligns with the Oracle Retail Merchandising System department hierarchy.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module

attributes.name: distribution_channel
attributes.description: The distribution channel for which this financial plan is scoped: DTC (Direct-to-Consumer) retail stores, DTC e-commerce, wholesale partnerships, or outlet stores. Drives channel-specific pricing strategy and inventory allocation.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Salesforce Commerce Cloud; Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: Fiscal quarter or period identifier within the fiscal year to which this plan applies (e.g., FY2025-Q1). Supports quarterly OTB budget reviews and financial reporting.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The company's fiscal year to which this merchandise financial plan belongs. May differ from calendar year depending on the company's fiscal calendar (e.g., fiscal year ending January 31).

attributes.name: is_locked
attributes.description: Indicates whether this merchandise financial plan has been locked and frozen for execution. When True, no further edits are permitted and the plan serves as the official baseline for OTB budget management and performance tracking.

attributes.name: plan_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this merchandise financial plan within Anaplan and Oracle Retail Merchandising System. Used for cross-system reconciliation and business reference.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: plan_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the planning period covered by this merchandise financial plan. Marks the end of the season's selling window and the EOM (End of Month) inventory target date.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: plan_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the merchandise financial plan, typically including season, year, department, and channel (e.g., 'FW2025 Womens Apparel DTC Retail Plan').

attributes.name: plan_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the planning period covered by this merchandise financial plan. Marks the beginning of the season's selling window for OTB and inventory planning purposes.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the merchandise financial plan. Draft indicates work-in-progress; submitted indicates pending approval; approved indicates finance/merchant sign-off; locked indicates frozen for execution; archived indicates superseded.

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the plan was generated using a top-down (executive-driven targets cascaded down), bottom-up (buyer/planner-driven builds rolled up), or reconciled (merged top-down and bottom-up) planning approach.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: plan_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the merchandise financial plan (e.g., v1.0, v2.3). Supports iterative planning cycles where plans are revised across pre-season, in-season, and post-season phases.

attributes.name: planned_aur
attributes.description: Planned AUR (Average Unit Retail) representing the expected average selling price per unit across the department/class/channel combination. Drives unit sales plan derivation from the net sales dollar plan.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management

attributes.name: planned_bop_inventory_amt
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Beginning of Period (BOP) Inventory Amount
attributes.description: Planned inventory value at retail at the beginning of the planning period. Used as the opening stock position for OTB calculations and inventory flow modeling.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_cogs_amt
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Amount
attributes.description: Planned COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) for the season, representing the total cost of merchandise expected to be sold. Used to derive planned gross margin and GMROI targets.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; IFRS/GAAP; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO

attributes.name: planned_eop_inventory_amt
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned End of Period (EOP) Inventory Amount
attributes.description: Planned inventory value at retail at the end of the planning period (EOM). Represents the target closing stock position and feeds into the next season's BOP. Critical for OTB and WOS (Weeks of Supply) planning.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_gmroi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI)
attributes.description: Planned GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) representing the gross margin dollars generated per dollar of average inventory investment. Core KPI for evaluating merchandise productivity and capital efficiency.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_gross_margin_amt
attributes.description: Planned gross margin in absolute dollar terms (planned net sales minus planned COGS). Represents the financial contribution of the merchandise category before operating expenses.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; IFRS/GAAP

attributes.name: planned_gross_margin_pct
attributes.description: Planned gross margin expressed as a percentage of planned net sales (planned gross margin / planned net sales). Key KPI for merchandising performance and pricing strategy evaluation.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; IFRS/GAAP

attributes.name: planned_imu_pct
attributes.description: Planned IMU (Initial Markup) percentage representing the difference between the cost of merchandise and its original retail price, expressed as a percentage of retail. Establishes the pricing floor before markdowns.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management

attributes.name: planned_inventory_turns
attributes.description: Planned number of times inventory is expected to sell through and be replenished during the season (COGS / average inventory at cost). Drives OTB budget and receipt flow planning.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_markdown_amt
attributes.description: Total planned markdown (MD) dollars for the season representing the anticipated reduction from original retail price to drive sell-through. Directly impacts MMU and gross margin performance.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management

attributes.name: planned_markdown_pct
attributes.description: Planned markdown as a percentage of planned net sales. Used to benchmark markdown aggressiveness across departments and channels and to set MMU expectations.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management

attributes.name: planned_mmu_pct
attributes.description: Planned MMU (Maintained Markup) percentage representing the actual markup achieved after markdowns and promotions, expressed as a percentage of net sales. Reflects the realized pricing performance versus IMU.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management

attributes.name: planned_msrp_avg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Average Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MSRP)
attributes.description: Planned average MSRP (Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price) across the SKUs in this department/class/channel plan. Establishes the retail price anchor for IMU calculation and consumer-facing pricing.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management; FTC Textile and Apparel Labeling Requirements

attributes.name: planned_net_sales_amt
attributes.description: Total planned net sales revenue (gross sales minus returns and allowances) for the season, department, class, and channel combination. Core financial target in the merchandise financial plan. Expressed in the plan's currency.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; IFRS/GAAP; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_otb_amt
attributes.description: Planned OTB (Open-to-Buy) budget in dollars representing the amount of merchandise the buyer is authorized to purchase for the season. Calculated as planned EOP inventory + planned sales + planned markdowns - planned BOP inventory.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_receipts_amt
attributes.description: Total planned merchandise receipts (inbound inventory) at retail value for the season. Represents the planned flow of new inventory into the channel to support the sales plan.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System; SAP S/4HANA MM

attributes.name: planned_str_pct
attributes.description: Planned STR (Sell-Through Rate) expressed as a percentage of units sold versus units received. Target sell-through rate used to calibrate buy quantities, markdown timing, and end-of-season inventory positions.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_units_sold
attributes.description: Total planned number of units expected to be sold during the season for the department/class/channel combination. Derived from planned net sales divided by planned AUR. Feeds into allocation and replenishment planning.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planned_wos
attributes.description: Planned WOS (Weeks of Supply) representing the number of weeks the current inventory position is expected to last at the planned rate of sale. Used to identify over/under-stock risk and trigger replenishment actions.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: planning_horizon
attributes.description: Indicates the planning phase this plan represents: pre-season (initial buy plan before season starts), in-season (revised plan during active selling), or post-season (actuals reconciliation and hindsight).
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: pricing_strategy
attributes.description: Planned pricing strategy for this channel and merchandise category: full_price (MSRP-driven), promotional (planned promotional events), value (everyday low price positioning), or outlet (clearance/off-price). Informs IMU and MMU targets.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management; Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this merchandise financial plan record was last modified. Tracks iterative plan revisions across pre-season, in-season, and post-season planning cycles.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5; Anaplan Merchandise Financial Planning Module

products.name: size_curve
products.description: Size curve profile master defining the expected unit sales distribution across size runs (alpha: XS/S/M/L/XL/XXL, numeric: 28-42, shoe: 5-14) for a style, merchandise class, or product category by channel, region, and store cluster. Captures curve type (standard, fitted, oversized), historical sell-through basis period, confidence level, and seasonal adjustment factors. Used to optimize buy plan size ratios, allocation size breaks, replenishment size packs, and initial distribution. Critical for minimizing size-related markdowns and stockouts in apparel where size fragmentation drives 15-20% of excess inventory. Managed in Oracle Retail and Anaplan.

attributes.name: size_curve_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the size curve profile record in the merchandising system. Primary key for the size_curve data product. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — this is a planning reference resource defining expected unit sales distribution across size runs.

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Size curves are often season-specific (seasonal adjustment factors, basis periods); season_code exists but no FK to season master. Adding season_id FK normalizes season reference and removes redundant

attributes.name: size_scale_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.size_scale. Business justification: Size curves define percentage distributions across size ranges and must reference the actual size scale (XS-XXL, numeric, etc.) to be operationally meaningful. Allocation planning requires mapping cur

attributes.name: basis_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the historical sell-through data period used to derive this size curve's distribution percentages. Together with basis_period_start_date, defines the historical window for statistical calibration of size ratios.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: basis_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the historical sell-through data period used to derive this size curve's distribution percentages. Defines the lookback window for statistical calibration. Typically covers 1-3 prior seasons of comparable selling history.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The distribution channel for which this size curve is calibrated. Size distributions differ materially by channel — e-commerce tends to over-index on extreme sizes (XS, XL) versus retail stores. DTC (Direct-to-Consumer) curves may differ from wholesale curves. Drives channel-specific buy plan size ratios.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Salesforce Commerce Cloud

attributes.name: class_code
attributes.description: Merchandise class code within the department hierarchy from Oracle Retail (e.g., 'WOVEN_TOPS', 'SLIM_FIT_JEANS'). A size curve may be defined at class level for more granular distribution accuracy. Aligns with Oracle Retail Merchandising System class hierarchy.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level of the size curve based on the volume and quality of historical sell-through data used in derivation. High confidence curves are used directly in buy plans; low confidence curves require planner override review. Drives curve applicability flags in Anaplan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this size curve record was first created in the system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX) per platform conventions.

attributes.name: curve_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the size curve profile, used in Oracle Retail Merchandising System and Anaplan for cross-system reference. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: curve_derivation_method
attributes.description: Method used to derive the size distribution percentages for this curve. Historical STR uses actual sell-through data; planner_override reflects manual planner judgment; vendor_recommended uses supplier-provided size ratios; statistical_model uses algorithmic forecasting; blended combines multiple methods. Affects confidence level assignment.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: curve_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the size curve profile (e.g., 'Women's Fitted Tops Standard', 'Men's Denim 28-42 Bell Curve'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity. Used in Oracle Retail and Anaplan planning interfaces.

attributes.name: curve_type
attributes.description: Classification of the size curve profile indicating the fit and silhouette category that drives the distribution shape. Standard curves follow bell-curve distributions; fitted curves skew toward smaller sizes; oversized curves skew toward larger sizes. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|fitted|oversized|petite|plus|tall|slim|relaxed — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Centric PLM Collection Management

attributes.name: department_code
attributes.description: Merchandise department code from Oracle Retail hierarchy (e.g., 'WOMENS_TOPS', 'MENS_DENIM', 'FOOTWEAR'). Defines the merchandise department scope for which this size curve is applicable. Used in assortment planning and OTB budget allocation.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date after which this size curve profile is no longer active for new planning runs. Null indicates an open-ended curve with no planned expiry. Used to manage curve versioning and seasonal transitions in Oracle Retail and Anaplan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this size curve profile becomes effective for use in buy planning, allocation, and replenishment. Curves are versioned by effective date to support seasonal transitions and curve updates without disrupting in-flight planning cycles.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: is_default_for_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: Is Default Curve for Merchandise Class
attributes.description: Indicates whether this size curve is the default curve applied to new styles within the associated merchandise class when no style-specific curve exists. True = default fallback curve for the class. Used in Oracle Retail automated allocation and buy plan generation.

attributes.name: is_replenishment_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this size curve is approved for use in automated replenishment size pack calculations in Manhattan Associates WMS. True = curve can drive replenishment size breaks. False = curve is restricted to initial buy plan and allocation use only.
attributes.references: Manhattan Associates WMS; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: Date on which this size curve was last reviewed and validated by a merchandise planner. Curves not reviewed within a defined period (e.g., 2 seasons) are flagged for re-validation to ensure continued accuracy. Supports governance of curve quality.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: markdown_risk_index
attributes.description: Composite risk score (0.00-100.00) indicating the likelihood of size-related markdown exposure if this curve is applied to a buy plan. Derived from historical size fragmentation patterns and STR variance across sizes. Higher scores indicate greater markdown risk from size imbalance. Critical for GMROI optimization.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for merchandise planner annotations regarding this size curve, including rationale for manual overrides, known anomalies in the historical basis data, or special instructions for application. Supports planning governance and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: numeric_size_distribution
attributes.description: Serialized representation of the size distribution percentages for numeric size runs (waist sizes 28-42 or equivalent), stored as a delimited string of size:percentage pairs (e.g., '28:5.0|30:12.0|32:22.0|34:25.0|36:18.0|38:12.0|40:4.0|42:2.0'). Null for alpha or shoe size scale types. Used when the number of numeric sizes exceeds the available discrete percentage columns.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: pct_l
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total unit sales allocated to size L in the alpha size run. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 25.00 = 25%). Null for numeric or shoe size scale types. Used in buy plan size ratio calculations and replenishment size pack optimization.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: pct_m
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total unit sales allocated to size M in the alpha size run. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 28.00 = 28%). Typically the modal size in standard bell-curve distributions. Null for numeric or shoe size scale types.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: pct_s
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total unit sales allocated to size S in the alpha size run. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 18.00 = 18%). Null for numeric or shoe size scale types. Used in buy plan size ratio calculations and allocation size breaks.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: pct_xl
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total unit sales allocated to size XL in the alpha size run. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 14.00 = 14%). Null for numeric or shoe size scale types. Used in buy plan size ratio calculations and initial distribution planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: pct_xs
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total unit sales allocated to size XS in the alpha size run. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 8.50 = 8.5%). Null for numeric or shoe size scale types. All size distribution percentages must sum to 100.00 for a valid curve. Serves as the principal MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE for this MASTER_RESOURCE.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: pct_xxl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Double Extra Large (XXL) Size Distribution Percentage
attributes.description: Expected percentage of total unit sales allocated to size XXL in the alpha size run. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 6.50 = 6.5%). Null for numeric or shoe size scale types. Monitoring XXL distribution is critical for plus-size assortment planning and markdown minimization.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: region_code
attributes.description: Geographic region for which this size curve applies (e.g., 'NA', 'EMEA', 'APAC', 'LATAM'). Size distributions vary significantly by region due to demographic differences. Used to apply region-specific size ratios in allocation and buy planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: reviewed_by
attributes.description: Name or user identifier of the merchandise planner who last reviewed and validated this size curve. Provides accountability for curve quality and supports audit trail requirements for merchandise planning governance.

attributes.name: sample_unit_count
attributes.description: Total number of units sold in the historical basis period used to derive this size curve. Higher sample counts yield higher statistical confidence. Used to validate confidence_level assignment — curves based on fewer than a threshold number of units are flagged as low confidence.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: seasonal_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Multiplicative adjustment factor applied to the base size distribution percentages to account for seasonal demand shifts (e.g., 1.0500 = 5% upward adjustment). Captures known seasonal size preference changes such as outerwear seasons skewing larger. Applied in Anaplan seasonal buy plan calculations.
attributes.references: Anaplan Merchandise Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: shoe_size_distribution
attributes.description: Serialized representation of the size distribution percentages for shoe size runs (US sizes 5-14 or equivalent), stored as a delimited string of size:percentage pairs (e.g., '7:8.0|7.5:10.0|8:15.0|8.5:18.0|9:17.0|9.5:14.0|10:12.0|10.5:6.0'). Null for alpha or numeric apparel size scale types.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: size_count
attributes.description: Total number of discrete sizes in the size run covered by this curve (e.g., 6 for XS-XXL alpha, 8 for 28-42 even numeric). Drives the number of size break columns populated in allocation and replenishment size pack calculations.

attributes.name: size_curve_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the size curve profile. Active curves are used in live buy plans and allocation runs. Draft curves are under development. Archived curves are retained for historical analysis but excluded from new planning cycles. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.

attributes.name: size_range_max
attributes.description: The largest size in the size run covered by this curve (e.g., 'XXL', '42', '14'). Combined with size_range_min to define the full size run span. Used to validate that buy plan size breaks fall within the defined range.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; ISO 8559-1 Clothing Size Designation

attributes.name: size_range_min
attributes.description: The smallest size in the size run covered by this curve (e.g., 'XS', '28', '5'). Combined with size_range_max to define the full size run span. Used to validate that buy plan size breaks fall within the defined range.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; ISO 8559-1 Clothing Size Designation

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this size curve record originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer. Oracle Retail is the primary system of record; Anaplan is used for planning-layer curves; Centric PLM may provide initial vendor-recommended curves.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning; Centric PLM

attributes.name: store_cluster_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the store cluster or store tier to which this size curve applies (e.g., 'FLAGSHIP', 'MALL_A', 'OUTLET_B'). Store clusters group locations with similar size-selling patterns. Enables cluster-level size allocation optimization to reduce size-related markdowns.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; SAP Customer Activity Repository

attributes.name: str_basis_pct
attributes.description: The minimum Sell-Through Rate (STR) achieved in the historical basis period for the data to be considered statistically valid for curve derivation. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 75.00 means 75% STR). Curves derived from low-STR periods may be flagged as low-confidence.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: subclass_code
attributes.description: Merchandise subclass code within the class hierarchy from Oracle Retail. Enables the most granular level of size curve definition when size distributions differ within a class (e.g., 'STRETCH_WOVEN' vs 'NON_STRETCH_WOVEN' within WOVEN_TOPS).

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this size curve record was last modified. Tracks the most recent update to any attribute of the size curve profile. Used for incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer and for audit trail purposes.

products.name: season
products.description: Merchandise season master reference defining trading seasons (Spring/Summer, Fall/Winter, Resort, Pre-Fall, Holiday, Cruise) with start and end dates, delivery windows, market week dates, T&A calendar milestones, financial planning periods, and markdown cadence calendar. Every planning entity in the merchandising domain (assortment, collection, OTB, buy plan, allocation, MFP) references a season as its temporal anchor. Serves as the canonical time-boundary definition for merchandise planning cycles. Managed in Oracle Retail Merchandising System.

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the merchandise season record. Primary key for the season master reference table in the merchandising domain.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Master

attributes.name: carbon_target_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sustainability.carbon_target. Business justification: Seasonal collections align with annual carbon reduction targets. Merchandisers plan seasons to contribute to company-wide carbon goals, tracking emissions from materials, production, and logistics aga

attributes.name: standard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.quality_standard. Business justification: Seasonal quality standards vary by delivery window, market regulations, and brand strategy. Standards are versioned by season for compliance tracking. Essential for seasonal quality planning and regul

attributes.name: target_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sustainability.sustainability_target. Business justification: Seasons track broader sustainability goals beyond carbon (water, waste, circularity). Merchandisers plan seasonal targets for sustainable material percentage, water reduction, and circular design prin

attributes.name: channel_scope
attributes.description: The distribution channel scope for which this season is planned. 'All' covers all channels; 'DTC' covers direct-to-consumer retail and e-commerce; 'Wholesale' covers wholesale and distribution partners. Drives channel-specific OTB allocation and assortment planning in Oracle Retail Merchandising System.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Assortment Planning; Salesforce Commerce Cloud

attributes.name: clearance_end_date
attributes.description: The date by which all clearance selling for this season must be completed. After this date, remaining inventory is subject to return-to-vendor (RTV), off-price channel transfer, or write-off. Defines the final boundary of the season's sell-through window.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Price Management; SAP S/4HANA MM

attributes.name: collection_theme
attributes.description: The creative or commercial theme name assigned to this season's collection (e.g., 'Urban Explorer', 'Coastal Luxe'). Defined during collection planning in Centric PLM and used to align product design, marketing campaigns, and visual merchandising narratives.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this season record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and record lifecycle tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity and Accountability

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all monetary planning amounts for this season are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Ensures consistent financial reporting across multi-currency operations in SAP S/4HANA FI/CO and Anaplan.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The official last trading date of the merchandise season — the date on which the season's assortment is retired from active selling. Defines the close of the OTB budget window and triggers end-of-season markdown cadence and clearance planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Calendar

attributes.name: first_delivery_date
attributes.description: The earliest scheduled date for merchandise receipts into the distribution center or stores for this season. Defines the opening of the delivery window and is a key milestone in the Time and Action (T&A) calendar for sourcing and procurement coordination.
attributes.references: Centric PLM — T&A Calendar; Manhattan Associates WMS — Inbound Planning

attributes.name: fiscal_half
attributes.description: The fiscal half-year period (H1 or H2) to which this season is aligned. Spring/Summer and Resort seasons typically fall in H1; Fall/Winter, Pre-Fall, and Holiday seasons in H2. Used for semi-annual merchandise financial planning (MFP) and OTB budget allocation in Anaplan.
attributes.references: Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year to which this season belongs for financial planning and reporting purposes (e.g., 2025). Aligns season-level OTB budgets and merchandise financial plans (MFP) to the corporate fiscal calendar in Anaplan and SAP S/4HANA FI/CO.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO — Fiscal Year; IFRS/GAAP Reporting Standards

attributes.name: gender_target
attributes.description: The primary gender target classification for this season's collection, used to segment assortment planning, allocation strategies, and marketing campaigns. Aligns with product hierarchy classifications in Oracle Retail Merchandising System and Centric PLM.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Assortment Planning; Centric PLM — Collection Management

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether this season is currently active and available for use in planning, buying, and allocation transactions. Set to True when the season status is 'active'; False for planning, closed, or archived seasons. Used to filter active seasons in Oracle Retail Merchandising System and Anaplan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Master

attributes.name: is_nos
attributes.business_glossary_term: Is Never Out of Stock (NOS) Season Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this season includes a Never Out of Stock (NOS) or carry-over program, where core styles are replenished continuously regardless of seasonal boundaries. NOS seasons require separate OTB budget allocation and replenishment planning in Oracle Retail Merchandising System.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Assortment Planning

attributes.name: last_delivery_date
attributes.description: The latest permissible date for merchandise receipts for this season. Defines the close of the delivery window. Receipts after this date may be subject to late delivery penalties or cancellation per vendor agreements. Key milestone in the T&A calendar.
attributes.references: Centric PLM — T&A Calendar; SAP S/4HANA MM — Purchase Order Management

attributes.name: markdown_cadence
attributes.description: The planned frequency of markdown (MD) events during the clearance phase of this season. Drives the markdown calendar in Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management and informs maintained markup (MMU) forecasting in Anaplan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Price Management; Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning

attributes.name: markdown_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the first planned markdown (MD) event for this season begins. Initiates the end-of-season clearance cadence. Drives markdown (MD) planning in Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management and Anaplan merchandise financial planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Price Management; Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning

attributes.name: market_week_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the industry market week associated with this season. Together with market_week_start_date, defines the window during which wholesale buyers finalize orders and assortment commitments.
attributes.references: Apparel industry market week calendar standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: market_week_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the industry market week (trade show / buying week) associated with this season, during which buyers review collections and place wholesale orders. Key date for collection planning and wholesale distribution calendars.
attributes.references: Apparel industry market week calendar standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: mfp_version
attributes.description: The version identifier of the approved merchandise financial plan (MFP) associated with this season in Anaplan (e.g., 'v1.0-Initial', 'v2.1-Revised'). Tracks plan revisions through the planning cycle and ensures alignment between OTB budgets and financial targets.

attributes.name: num_planned_skus
attributes.business_glossary_term: Number of Planned Stock Keeping Units (SKUs)
attributes.description: The total number of distinct SKUs (Stock Keeping Units) planned for this season across all styles, colors, and sizes. Used to manage assortment breadth, warehouse capacity planning in Manhattan Associates WMS, and OTB unit buy planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Assortment Planning; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: num_planned_styles
attributes.description: The total number of distinct styles (SKU parent-level products) planned for this season's assortment. Set during collection planning in Centric PLM and used to manage line architecture, OTB depth-versus-breadth trade-offs, and assortment productivity analysis.
attributes.references: Centric PLM — Collection Management; Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Assortment Planning

attributes.name: order_deadline_date
attributes.description: The final date by which all purchase orders (POs) for this season must be submitted to suppliers to ensure on-time delivery within the season's delivery window. Critical T&A calendar milestone managed in SAP S/4HANA MM and Centric PLM.
attributes.references: Centric PLM — T&A Calendar; SAP S/4HANA MM — Purchase Order Management

attributes.name: otb_budget_amount
attributes.description: The total approved Open-to-Buy (OTB) budget in the company's reporting currency for this season. Represents the maximum planned merchandise spend authorized for buying activities. Set during merchandise financial planning (MFP) in Anaplan and tracked against actual PO commitments in Oracle Retail Merchandising System.
attributes.references: Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System — OTB

attributes.name: planned_gross_margin_pct
attributes.description: The planned gross margin percentage for this season as set in the merchandise financial plan (MFP). Calculated as (planned sales minus planned cost of goods sold) divided by planned sales. Drives GMROI targets and IMU/MMU planning in Anaplan.

attributes.name: planned_imu_pct
attributes.description: The planned initial markup (IMU) percentage for this season, representing the difference between the cost of goods and the initial retail price (MSRP) as a percentage of retail. Set during merchandise financial planning and used to guide pricing strategy in Oracle Retail Merchandising System Price Management.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Price Management; Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning

attributes.name: planned_sales_amount
attributes.description: The total planned net sales revenue in the company's reporting currency for this season as set during merchandise financial planning (MFP). Serves as the top-line revenue target against which actual sell-through rate (STR) and average unit retail (AUR) performance are measured.
attributes.references: Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning; IFRS/GAAP Revenue Recognition Standards

attributes.name: planned_str_pct
attributes.description: The planned sell-through rate (STR) percentage target for this season, representing the proportion of received inventory expected to be sold at full price before markdown. Used to benchmark actual in-season performance and trigger markdown cadence decisions.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Assortment Planning; Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning

attributes.name: planning_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which internal merchandise planning activities formally begin for this season, including OTB budget setting, assortment planning, and buy plan development in Anaplan and Oracle Retail Merchandising System. Precedes the trading start date by several months.
attributes.references: Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: pre_production_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which pre-production (PP) activities commence for this season, including fabric and trim approvals, fit samples, and pre-production sample sign-off. Key milestone in the T&A calendar tracked in Centric PLM and Infor PLM.
attributes.references: Centric PLM — Collection Management; Infor PLM — BOM Management

attributes.name: region_scope
attributes.description: The geographic region or market scope for which this season is defined (e.g., 'Global', 'North America', 'EMEA', 'APAC'). Supports multi-regional merchandise planning where season start/end dates and delivery windows may vary by market. Used in Oracle Retail Merchandising System and Anaplan regional planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Master; Anaplan — Merchandise Financial Planning

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the season across all planning and operational systems (e.g., SS25, FW24, HO24, RES25). Used as the business key in Oracle Retail Merchandising System, Anaplan, and Centric PLM for cross-system season referencing.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Master; Centric PLM — Collection Management

attributes.name: season_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description of the season, capturing key strategic intent, collection positioning, target consumer profile, or planning notes. Used by merchandising and planning teams for context in Oracle Retail Merchandising System and Anaplan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Master

attributes.name: season_name
attributes.description: Human-readable full name of the merchandise season (e.g., 'Spring/Summer 2025', 'Fall/Winter 2024', 'Holiday 2024', 'Resort 2025'). Used in reporting, planning dashboards, and buyer-facing documents.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Master

attributes.name: season_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the merchandise season. 'planning' indicates the season is in pre-production planning; 'active' indicates the season is currently trading; 'closed' indicates the season has ended trading; 'archived' indicates the season is retained for historical reference only. Controls visibility in planning tools and reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Lifecycle

attributes.name: season_type
attributes.description: Classification of the trading season by industry-standard merchandise calendar type. Drives collection planning, OTB budget cycles, and markdown cadence. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Spring/Summer|Fall/Winter|Resort|Pre-Fall|Holiday|Cruise — promote to reference product if additional season types are introduced]
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Classification; Apparel industry merchandise calendar standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this season record was sourced (e.g., ORM = Oracle Retail Merchandising System, ANAPLAN = Anaplan, CENTRIC = Centric PLM). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; Anaplan; Centric PLM

attributes.name: source_system_season_code
attributes.description: The native season identifier as recorded in the originating operational system of record (e.g., Oracle Retail Merchandising System season number, Anaplan season key). Enables traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver Layer and source systems.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Master; Anaplan

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The official first trading date of the merchandise season — the date on which the season's assortment becomes available for sale in retail stores and e-commerce channels. Serves as the temporal anchor for all season-level planning entities including assortment, OTB, allocation, and MFP.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Season Calendar

attributes.name: tna_calendar_code
attributes.description: Reference code linking this season to its associated Time and Action (T&A) calendar template in Centric PLM or Infor PLM. The T&A calendar defines all critical path milestones from design brief through to final delivery for the season.
attributes.references: Centric PLM — T&A Calendar; Infor PLM — Sourcing

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this season record was last modified in the data platform. Used to detect changes, support incremental data loads, and maintain audit trail compliance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity and Accountability

attributes.name: weeks_of_supply_target
attributes.description: The target number of weeks of supply (WOS) to be maintained during the peak trading period of this season. Used to calibrate inventory depth in buy plans and allocation strategies, ensuring sufficient stock without excess inventory build-up.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System — Allocation; Anaplan — Demand Planning

products.name: price_change_event
products.description: Transactional record of any retail price modification event including permanent markdowns, temporary markdowns, markups, clearance pricing, and promotional price changes applied to a style or SKU

attributes.name: price_change_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each price change event record in the merchandising system. Primary key for the price_change_event data product.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Markdown decisions are tracked against cost center budgets for accountability. Finance requires this link to allocate markdown expenses to responsible cost centers and monitor markdown budget consumpt

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or merchandising manager who authorized and approved this price change event. Supports governance and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Fair Labor Association (FLA)

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Price changes post to specific GL accounts (markdown expense, inventory reserve, promotional allowance). Finance requires this link to automate GL posting of markdown events and ensure proper expense

attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_incident. Business justification: Price changes may result from compliance incidents (product recalls, safety violations requiring clearance, labeling corrections); incident triggers markdown and links event to root cause for financia

attributes.name: markdown_budget_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Open-to-Buy (OTB) markdown budget allocation against which this price change event is charged. Links the price change to the merchandise financial plan managed in Anaplan.
attributes.references: Anaplan - Merchandise Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: marketing_campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign. Business justification: Price changes (especially markdowns) are often timed to marketing campaigns. This link tracks which campaign drove the pricing decision, enabling analysis of campaign-driven markdown effectiveness and

attributes.name: non_conformance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.non_conformance. Business justification: Quality NCRs trigger clearance markdowns and vendor chargebacks. NCR documentation justifies markdown budget usage and supports vendor debit memos. Critical for linking quality failures to financial i

attributes.name: price_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.price_master. Business justification: Price change events modify prices; price_master is the authoritative source for pricing data. Adding price_master_id FK links transactional price changes to master pricing records and removes redundan

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Markdowns impact profit center margin performance. Financial reporting requires linking markdown events to profit centers to measure margin erosion by channel/brand and assess merchandising effectiven

attributes.name: promotion_id
attributes.description: Reference to the promotional campaign or event that triggered this price change, if applicable. Links promotional price changes to the originating marketing or merchandising promotion.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: retail_store_id
attributes.description: Reference to the retail store, channel, or distribution location where this price change event is effective. Supports location-specific pricing strategies across DTC, wholesale, and e-commerce channels.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; SAP Customer Activity Repository

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) to which this price change event applies. A SKU represents the most granular sellable unit (style-color-size combination).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: style_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent style (product) to which this price change event applies. A price change may be applied at the style level and cascade to all associated SKUs.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: vendor_allowance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.vendor_allowance. Business justification: Price change events (markdowns) may be funded by vendor allowances (markdown money). Adding vendor_allowance_id FK links markdown execution to vendor funding source. FK will reference merchandising.ve

attributes.name: vendor_cost_quote_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sourcing.vendor_cost_quote. Business justification: Markdown decisions consider original vendor costs from quotes to assess margin impact and determine vendor allowance eligibility. Critical for markdown planning, vendor negotiation for markdown suppor

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the price change event was formally approved by the authorized merchandising manager or buyer. Required for governance compliance and audit trail in Oracle Retail Merchandising System.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; IFRS/GAAP

attributes.name: change_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized reason code from Oracle Retail Merchandising System explaining the business rationale for the price change (e.g., SEASONAL_MD, COMPETITIVE_RESPONSE, CLEARANCE, PROMO, CORRECTION). Supports markdown (MD) analysis and GMROI reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: change_reason_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description providing additional context for the price change event beyond the standardized reason code. Entered by the merchandising planner or buyer.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: change_type
attributes.description: Classification of the price change event by its business purpose. Permanent Markdown (MD) reduces the retail price indefinitely; Temporary Markdown is time-bound; Markup (MU) increases price; Clearance applies end-of-season liquidation pricing; Promotional applies campaign-driven pricing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: permanent_markdown|temporary_markdown|markup|clearance|promotional — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The sales channel to which this price change event applies. Supports channel-specific pricing strategies across Direct-to-Consumer (DTC), wholesale, retail store, e-commerce (Salesforce Commerce Cloud), and outlet channels.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Salesforce Commerce Cloud

attributes.name: class_code
attributes.description: The merchandise class code within the department hierarchy for the affected SKU or style. Used for class-level markdown (MD) analysis and GMROI optimization in Anaplan merchandise financial planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Assortment Planning

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this price change event record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: IFRS/GAAP Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the price change amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Supports multi-currency retail operations across international markets.

attributes.name: department_code
attributes.description: The merchandise department classification code for the SKU or style affected by this price change event. Aligns with Oracle Retail Merchandising System department hierarchy for assortment planning and OTB reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Assortment Planning

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the new price becomes active and visible to customers across applicable channels. Used for scheduling future price changes in advance.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the price change expires and the price reverts to the prior or next scheduled price. Null for permanent price changes. Critical for temporary markdowns and promotional pricing.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the price change event within the Oracle Retail Merchandising System workflow. Drives whether the price change is visible and applied at POS and e-commerce channels.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise real-world date and time when the price change event was executed or became effective in the system of record. This is the principal business event time, distinct from audit timestamps.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: imu_percent
attributes.description: The Initial Markup (IMU) percentage for the affected SKU or style at the time of this price change event. Represents the original margin built into the retail price relative to cost. Used to assess markdown (MD) impact on maintained markup (MMU).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: is_clearance
attributes.description: Indicates whether this price change event designates the SKU or style as a clearance item. Once flagged as clearance, the item is typically excluded from future regular-price replenishment and tracked separately for end-of-season liquidation reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: is_competitive_response
attributes.description: Indicates whether this price change event was triggered by a competitive pricing response to a market competitor's price action. Supports competitive pricing analytics and brand positioning strategy.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: is_pos_applied
attributes.business_glossary_term: Is Point of Sale (POS) Applied Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this price change event has been successfully transmitted and applied at the Point of Sale (POS) system via SAP Customer Activity Repository. Supports reconciliation between merchandising system and store operations.
attributes.references: SAP Customer Activity Repository - POS; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: markdown_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential number indicating the ordinal position of this markdown (MD) event within the seasonal markdown cadence for the affected SKU or style (e.g., 1st markdown, 2nd markdown, 3rd markdown). Supports sell-through rate (STR) analysis and markdown optimization.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: mmu_percent
attributes.description: The Maintained Markup (MMU) percentage for the affected SKU or style after applying this price change event. Reflects the actual margin achieved post-markdown or post-markup. Key metric for GMROI optimization.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: new_retail_price
attributes.description: The updated retail selling price applied to the SKU or style as a result of this price change event. Represents the Average Unit Retail (AUR) post-change and is used in sell-through rate (STR) and GMROI analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; IFRS/GAAP

attributes.name: original_retail_price
attributes.description: The retail selling price of the SKU or style immediately prior to this price change event. Serves as the baseline for calculating markdown (MD) depth, sell-through rate (STR) impact, and maintained markup (MMU).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; IFRS/GAAP

attributes.name: price_change_amount
attributes.description: The absolute monetary value of the price change (new_retail_price minus original_retail_price). A negative value indicates a markdown (MD); a positive value indicates a markup (MU). Used in merchandise financial planning and OTB impact analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: price_change_level
attributes.description: Indicates the merchandise hierarchy level at which this price change event was initiated. A style-level change cascades to all associated SKUs; a SKU-level change applies only to the specific variant.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: price_change_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the price change event as assigned by Oracle Retail Merchandising System or SAP S/4HANA SD module. Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit traceability.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: price_change_percent
attributes.description: The percentage change in retail price relative to the original retail price. Calculated as (price_change_amount / original_retail_price) * 100. Used for markdown (MD) depth reporting and sell-through rate (STR) analysis in Anaplan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: pricing_zone_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the geographic or channel-based pricing zone to which this price change event applies. Pricing zones group locations with identical pricing strategies in Oracle Retail Merchandising System.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Price Management

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: The merchandise season code (e.g., SS25, FW24) associated with the collection or buy plan for the affected SKU or style. Critical for seasonal markdown (MD) cadence management and end-of-season clearance pricing.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Assortment Planning; Anaplan Merchandise Planning

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated this price change event. Supports data lineage and cross-system reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System; SAP S/4HANA SD; Anaplan

attributes.name: str_at_change
attributes.description: The Sell-Through Rate (STR) for the affected SKU or style at the time of this price change event, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.65 = 65%). Provides context for the markdown decision and is used in post-event STR lift analysis.
attributes.references: Anaplan - Merchandise Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

attributes.name: subclass_code
attributes.description: The merchandise subclass code providing the most granular product hierarchy classification for the affected SKU or style. Supports subclass-level sell-through rate (STR) and markdown (MD) depth analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Assortment Planning

attributes.name: units_on_hand
attributes.description: The inventory quantity on hand for the affected SKU at the time of this price change event. Used to calculate the total markdown (MD) dollar exposure and weeks of supply (WOS) impact in merchandise financial planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System - Allocation; Manhattan Associates WMS

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this price change event record was last modified. Tracks amendments, corrections, or status updates to the price change event.
attributes.references: IFRS/GAAP Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: wos_at_change
attributes.business_glossary_term: Weeks of Supply (WOS) at Price Change
attributes.description: The Weeks of Supply (WOS) for the affected SKU at the time of this price change event, calculated as units on hand divided by average weekly sales rate. Used to assess inventory urgency and justify markdown (MD) depth decisions.
attributes.references: Anaplan - Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System

Captures vendor, allowance type, agreement terms, earned versus claimed amounts, accrual periods, claim submission deadlines, and settlement status. Critical for gross margin management and vendor negotiation leverage. Tracked in Oracle Retail Invoice Matching and SAP FI-MM.

attributes.name: corrective_action_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Vendor allowances post to specific GL accounts (vendor income, markdown offset, co-op advertising). Finance requires this link to automate GL posting of vendor allowance accruals and ensure proper inc

Adding merchandise_hierarchy_id FK normalizes merchandise classification and removes redundant hierarchy attri

attributes.name: order_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific purchase order (PO) associated with this allowance. Nullable if allowance is not PO-specific.

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Vendor allowances improve profit center margin performance. Financial reporting requires linking vendor allowance income to profit centers to measure net margin impact by channel/brand and assess vend

attributes.name: promotion_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.promotion. Business justification: Vendor allowances (co-op funds, markdown money) often support specific promotional events. Vendors provide financial allowances to fund markdowns, advertising, or promotional pricing for their product

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Vendor allowances are negotiated per season; season_code exists but no FK to season master. Adding season_id FK normalizes season reference and removes redundant season_code. FK will reference merchan

attributes.name: shipment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to logistics.logistics_shipment. Business justification: Vendor allowances (co-op, markdown support, freight claims) are often tied to specific shipment performance—late delivery penalties, damage claims, or duty refunds. Linking to shipment enables allowan

attributes.name: sourcing_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sourcing.sourcing_purchase_order. Essential for allowance claim validation, accrual tracking, and reconciliation of vendor funding

attributes.name: supplier_esg_assessment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sustainability.supplier_esg_assessment. Business justification: Vendor allowances are increasingly tied to ESG performance incentives (e.g., bonus allowances for achieving sustainability milestones). Buyers negotiate allowances based on supplier ESG scores to driv
